BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.

From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). # Project Kestrel: Buyer review of Seller Update and Disclosure Letter

**Preliminary point:** The "Reviewer Efficiency Note" says the [STANDARD] clauses are cleared by both sides and the disclosure and limitation package is accepted. That is the Seller's assertion, and nothing on our record supports it. We have not agreed any of these positions, so I have reviewed every item in full. We should say so in the cover email to avoid any argument that we accepted by silence.

**Fallbacks:** Two Seller positions (20% cap and 18-month period) match our fallbacks. Both need prior written authority from Amelia Frost identifying the draft, and none has been given. I have treated them as not available.

---

**SPA-N-001: General liability cap**
- **Seller:** 20% / AUD 4.8m (cl 12.1).
- **Buyer wants:** 25% / AUD 6.0m.
- **Recommendation:** Reject and counter at 25% / AUD 6.0m.
- **Reason:** The Seller has opened at our conditional fallback, which we cannot offer without Frost's written authority.

**SPA-N-002: De minimis and basket**
- **Seller:** De minimis AUD 25,000. Basket AUD 250,000, with only the excess recoverable (cl 12.2).
- **Buyer wants:** De minimis AUD 5,000. Basket AUD 50,000, with the Seller liable from the first dollar once exceeded.
- **Recommendation:** Reject and counter with our figures and tipping-basket mechanics.
- **Reason:** The Seller's thresholds are 5x ours and its deductible structure would remove most realistic claims.

**SPA-N-003: General claims time limit**
- **Seller:** 18 months, plus a clause applying "any limitation" to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise (cl 12.3/13).
- **Buyer wants:** 24 months for general claims. Fundamental and Title claims, and fraud, sit outside it.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Counter at 24 months and delete the blanket-application wording.
- **Reason:** 18 months is a fallback needing Frost's approval, and the blanket wording would cut across the Title and fraud regimes.

**SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime**
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties, "for administrative simplicity".
- **Buyer wants:** A separate regime with a 100% cap and at least six years. It sits outside the general basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
- **Recommendation:** Reject outright.
- **Reason:** Capping title at 20% of price on an 18-month clock would undermine the core of what we are buying.

**SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out**
- **Seller:** The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to "all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3/12.8/20.5), with no fraud carve-out.
- **Buyer wants:** Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable.
- **Recommendation:** Reject and insert an express carve-out in each of those clauses.
- **Reason:** This carve-out is non-waivable under our playbook, and the Seller's wording would shield its own fraud.

**SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope**
- **Seller:** General disclosure of the whole data room and public registers (Schedule 7; Disclosure Letter 1.1 and 1.2).
- **Buyer wants:** Specific, fair disclosure against identified warranties only.
- **Recommendation:** Reject 1.1 and 1.2 as deemed disclosure. Accept only specific disclosures. Qualify 1.4 so it does not limit warranty or indemnity claims.
- **Reason:** Whole-data-room and public-register disclosure would neutralise the warranties. The specific items in sections 2 to 10 of the letter are the useful part.

**SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier**
- **Seller:** No claim for anything the Buyer or its advisers knew, including anything discoverable from the data room or public records (cl 8.3).
- **Buyer wants:** Delete the clause.
- **Recommendation:** Delete cl 8.3. If a knowledge qualifier is unavoidable, limit it to named Seller knowledge persons with reasonable enquiry. It must never apply to title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- **Reason:** "Discoverable" knowledge combined with whole-data-room disclosure would exclude nearly every claim.

**SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent**
- **Seller:** Reasonable endeavours, with the consent treated as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent (cl 3/6.3).
- **Buyer wants:** An effective consent and evidence that its conditions are satisfied before Completion.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Make Bluefen a condition precedent requiring both the effective consent and evidence that the DD-002 cl 11.3 conditions are met.
- **Reason:** Bluefen is about 30% of revenue (about AUD 3.6m). The Seller's own letter admits there is no consent and no evidence of conditions, so "satisfied on delivery" would not protect us.

**SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility**
- **Seller:** Release to be provided after Completion (cl 2/7). About AUD 3.2m is outstanding.
- **Buyer wants:** A current payout figure, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective security releases at Completion.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the post-completion release. Require a payout letter, direct repayment through the funds flow, and releases delivered at Completion.
- **Reason:** The Seller's letter confirms the facility is unpaid and no discharge exists. A post-completion release would need an irrevocable undertaking and Frost's approval, and neither is in place.

**SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses**
- **Seller:** The AUD 420,000 DD-005 bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised in the funds flow.
- **Buyer wants:** The bonuses plus triggered on-costs shown as a specific line item, or expressly Seller-funded.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the silent exclusion. Require an express line item or Seller-funding covenant, and ask the Seller to confirm payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs.
- **Reason:** The Seller's letter says the amounts are not in the funds flow and does not address on-costs, so the Company would bear them post-Completion.

**SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity**
- **Seller:** The existing indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment and is "adequate" (cl 11.1).
- **Buyer wants:** A broader indemnity that preserves the SOW3 cure.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the narrow wording. Broaden the indemnity to cover Ironquay IP and ownership claims generally, keep the SOW3 payment cure, and request payment evidence or a confirmatory assignment.
- **Reason:** DD-004 cl 7.3 ties transfer of the materials to cleared payment. The AUD 180,000 is not independently verified in either direction, so we should not assume it is owed or paid.

**SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident (DD-006)**
- **Seller:** A preliminary operational matter, "not expected to be material" (cl 4.6/Sch 6).
- **Buyer wants:** Log preservation, a proper investigation and ongoing updates. No assumption of breach, harm, notification duty or dollar figure either way.
- **Recommendation:** Do not accept the "not material" characterisation. Require log preservation, an investigation with a defined scope, and prompt updates to us. Keep the matter open without asserting a breach.
- **Reason:** The Seller's own letter says access, scope and notification are undetermined, so neither "immaterial" nor "breach" is supported yet.

**SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals**
- **Seller:** Three renewals totalling AUD 330,000, described as ordinary-course operating costs.
- **Buyer wants:** An assessment, with no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
- **Recommendation:** Do not agree to either characterisation yet. Request the terms (terminability, accrual, timing, scope) and assess before taking a position.
- **Reason:** The letter does not say whether the renewals are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary-course, so neither side's label is established.

**SPA-N-014: Category separation**
- **Seller:** Blanket limitations and one general regime for all Claims.
- **Buyer wants:** Title, Tax, IP, payment and covenant categories kept separate, with no hidden general-regime override.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Restructure the draft with separate regimes, and add an express statement that the general limitations do not override them.
- **Reason:** The "all Claims of any nature" wording would pull every category into the general regime.

**SPA-N-015: Title verification**
- **Seller:** Title is evidenced by the Company's share register at DD-012.
- **Buyer wants:** Independent evidence of title, ownership, encumbrances and authority.
- **Recommendation:** Do not accept the register as proof. Require independent evidence, such as certified transfer history, ASIC and PPSR searches, and board and shareholder authority. Make title delivery a Completion deliverable.
- **Reason:** DD-012 is an internal source, and the Seller's own letter says it does not show the Buyer has verified title.

**SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms**
- **Seller:** Tax and IP are "settled under the general regime".
- **Buyer wants:** Both kept open and unresolved, with no assumption of unlimited liability.
- **Recommendation:** Reject "settled". Reserve both as open and negotiate them separately.
- **Reason:** Nothing has been agreed on tax or IP, and the general regime does not apply to them by default.

---

**Next steps:**
1. Send a mark-up that rejects the [STANDARD] label and counters on every item above.
2. If the deal team wants to trade down to the 20% cap or 18-month period, the request must go to Amelia Frost, identify the specific draft, and be approved in writing first.
3. Chase the outstanding evidence: the Bluefen consent and conditions, the Riverlark payout and discharge, the Ironquay payment evidence, the bonus on-costs, the Sandbar terms, the DD-006 investigation status, and independent title evidence.
